responses.content:
A reliable fact-checking query!

According to widely accepted sources, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Encyclopedia Britannica:

- The Pacific Ocean is the largest of the world's five oceans.
- It covers approximately 155.6 million square kilometers (60.1 million square miles).
- Its area accounts for about 46% to 48% of the Earth's ocean surface.

The Atlantic Ocean, while the second-largest ocean by volume, is not the largest when considering total surface area. The Southern Ocean (also known as the Antarctic Ocean) is often considered part of the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans, so its boundary can be somewhat ambiguous.

It is essential to note that the definition of an "ocean" can be somewhat subjective, but geographically, the oceans are usually defined by their boundaries. The International Hydrographic Organization (IHO), which is responsible for regulating the official names and boundaries of the world's oceans, considers the Atlantic Ocean to be a part of the Pacific Ocean.

So, while it is accurate to say that the Pacific Ocean covers approximately 46% of the Earth's ocean surface, the Atlantic Ocean as a distinct entity does not reach this threshold.
